# The two questions the clarify record deferred, answered

**How far the damage reached.** All thirteen journals were checked by reading record 1 and testing the
recorded path. One is stale: SEEN-096, whose file was renamed by its own three-way split. Every other
journal names a ticket that still exists, so no other score was taken against the wrong text. The fix
repairs one ticket and prevents the next.

**What SEEN-096's clarify record scores now.** Re-asked unchanged, through the fixed `state_for`, which
reports `found by id` and reads a ticket that no longer mentions repowise: **0.79**, against the 0.46 it
scored on the same record when the gate was reading the pre-split ticket.

That is 0.33 of pure measurement error, and it is still one hundredth short of the 0.8 threshold.

Both halves of that matter. The record was never as bad as the gate said, and it is not yet good
enough on its own terms either. SEEN-096 will need another attempt at its clarify record or a recorded
override, and now it will be judged against the ticket it is actually working. The number is written
down here so that when SEEN-096 unparks, nobody has to guess whether the fix was what moved it.
